deep: Vertex streams and declarations: validation order
The XNA stock effects: exact semantics, worked uses and verification history

set.summary: XNA refuses a draw whose vertex declaration lacks a semantic the shader reads; CNA has no device-level check, so EasyGL feeds neutral values, WEBGPU substitutes, SDL_GPU and FNA3D throw NotSupportedException and VULKAN aliases TEXCOORD1.
set.actual: GraphicsDevice::validateDrawState in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}} implements XNA's draw-time float-filtering and blending restrictions but no input check; no source under modules/ implements MissingVertexShaderInput. StockEffectUsesVertexSemantic in {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}} encodes the per-variant table but decides only which streams are consumed. EasyGL leaves a missing attribute disabled and reads the (0, 0, 0, 1) neutral record, except that a lit BasicEffect draw whose declaration names no Normal is now drawn unlit (StockLightingFollowsDeclarationEXT, AM4-056); WEBGPU's SelectStockVertexShapeEXT falls back from EnvironmentMapEffect without NORMAL0/TEXCOORD0 to a BasicEffect shape and sends alpha-test or dual-texture draws without TEXCOORD0 to the stride-16 coloured path; SDL_GPU throws NotSupportedException for those cases (std::invalid_argument for SkinnedEffect); VULKAN aliases TEXCOORD1 onto TEXCOORD0 for DualTextureEffect where the others read (0, 0). FNA3D, on every driver but OpenGL, now checks a stock draw against the inputs the selected XNA stock vertex shader reads and throws NotSupportedException naming the missing input (RequireStockVertexInputsDeclared in {{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dDraw.cpp|Fna3dDraw.cpp}}, AM4-190), because its Metal and SDL_GPU drivers otherwise fail the pipeline and crash; that is a renderer refusal with a different exception type, not XNA's device-level InvalidOperationException.

set.summary: DateTimeReader masks off the two kind bits and returns System::DateTime(ticks) with an unspecified kind, and it does not convert a Local-kind value to local time as XNA does. The header justifies the deviation by System::DateTime not modelling a kind, but System::DateTime has a (ticks, DateTimeKind) constructor at TARGET, so that reason is stale.
set.expected: XNA's DateTimeReader restores DateTimeKind from the top two bits and, for a Local value, converts the stored UTC ticks to local time (new DateTime(ticks, Utc).ToLocalTime()).
set.actual: {{src:modules/content/include/CNA/Internal/Xnb/DecimalDateTimeContentTypeReaders.hpp|DecimalDateTimeContentTypeReaders.hpp}} applies kindMask = 3 << 62 and returns System::DateTime(ticks). Its comment documents this as a deliberate deviation because System::DateTime 'does not store/track DateTimeKind at all'; that premise is out of date, since CNA's own XnaIntermediateSerializerTests builds Utc values with System::DateTime(ticks, System::DateTimeKind::Utc). The XNB writer in {{src:modules/content/src/Xnb/XnbBuiltInWriters.cpp|XnbBuiltInWriters.cpp}} likewise writes Unspecified. A Local-kind value therefore loads as its stored UTC ticks, without XNA's offset conversion.

set.title: Models built to .xnb carry no cameras, because an XNA Model has no camera storage
set.summary: A glTF compiled to .xnb drops its cameras with a build warning, so the model loads with an empty CamerasEXT; the direct glTF, .cnj and .cnb routes carry them, and Model.hpp still documents the property as empty for every other content path.
set.public_contract: Model::getCamerasEXTProperty() on models loaded through .xnb, .cnj and .cnb; the XNB model output of the content build
set.expected: A camera authored in the glTF source should survive whichever CNA route the model takes, as the other imported data (bones, clips, materials) does, or the route should say that it cannot carry it.
set.actual:
The direct glTF route fills Model::CamerasEXT (MakeModelCameraEXT in {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentModelLoaders.cpp|ContentModelLoaders.cpp}}). Since 1beef880d (CNA-DEMOS-ISSUE-023) {{src:tools/gltf_to_cnj/gltf_to_cnj.cpp|gltf_to_cnj}} writes the cameras into the Model .cnj, the .cnj reader carries them into CnbModelData::cameras, an optional MCAM chunk stores them in the .cnb, and both loaders build each camera through the same MakeModelCameraEXT. An .xnb model cannot hold them: XNA's Model has no camera member, so {{src:modules/content/src/Pipeline/XnbOutputContentPipeline.cpp|XnbOutputContentPipeline.cpp}} drops them with the warning “camera(s) are not written: an XNA Model has no camera storage”, and such a model loads with an empty CamerasEXT.

CNA closed ISSUE-023 on a complete checkpoint (6c8b042c4, 2026-10-24). {{src:modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Model.hpp|Model.hpp}} still documents the property as “Empty for every model built by any other content path”, which reads as if only the direct glTF route filled it.

set.actual: ContentManager.cpp logs, per mirrored placement, that CNA "does not reverse the triangle winding for it, so this placement's front faces are back-facing under the default cull mode", and GltfImportCore.cpp (AppendGltfInstanceReportEXT) records mirrored-winding-unapplied: "the application must reverse culling for this draw". The reason is architectural: the index and vertex buffers are shared with unmirrored placements of the same mesh, and cull state is per-draw device state. No public Model or ModelMesh property carries a per-mesh mirroring flag. The only public route is the Model's import report (Model::getGltfImportReportEXTProperty), which lists each mirrored placement by node name in a diagnostic whose Code is mirrored-winding-unapplied, so an application has to map that node name to the ModelMesh it draws, or recompute the determinant from the bone transforms.
set.workaround: Find the mirrored placements in the Model's import report (getGltfImportReportEXTProperty(), diagnostic mirrored-winding-unapplied, subject = node name), then draw such meshes with RasterizerState::CullNone, or detect a negative determinant of the absolute bone transform and switch to the opposite cull mode for that draw.

set.title: CUBICSPLINE bone and node channels are replayed linearly between samples taken at least every 1/60 s, an approximation of the authored curve
set.summary: BuildTrack samples each CUBICSPLINE interval at least every 1/60 s and AnimationPlayer lerps/slerps between the samples, so the curve between samples is approximated.
set.actual:
BuildTrack in {{src:modules/content/src/GltfImport/GltfImportCore.cpp|GltfImportCore.cpp}} resamples a bone's channels onto the union of their key times and, since a9d378c06, also samples every CUBICSPLINE interval at least every 1/60 s (four samples at the least) and adds a hold key 10 µs before each STEP key, each evaluated with the channel's own mode. SampleTrack in {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/AnimationPlayer.cpp|AnimationPlayer.cpp}} still interpolates linearly (Slerp for rotation) between those samples, so a CUBICSPLINE curve is piecewise-linear between samples rather than evaluated. {{src:docs/gltf-limitations.md|gltf-limitations.md}} records the result: anim-cubicspline plays within 0.0021 units of its spline (it was 0.962 off), “a bound for that fixture, not a universal one, because authored tangents may bend a spline more sharply”. Morph-weight tracks keep their tangents and are evaluated as Hermite curves.

The dense sampling is CNA's fix for CNA-DEMOS-ISSUE-031 (STEP and CUBICSPLINE playing as LINEAR), which CNA closed on a complete checkpoint (6c8b042c4, 2026-10-24); the approximation between samples is what remains.

set.title: LocalNetworkGamer::SendData in a Local or LocalWithLeaderboards session silently drops every packet, so neither the sender nor another local gamer ever receives it
set.summary: NetworkSession::Update raises PacketSend events only when real networking is enabled (SystemLink, or a service-backed PlayerMatch/Ranked session), so SendData in a Local or LocalWithLeaderboards session reports success and delivers nothing, although SendData is documented to reach every gamer in the session, the sender included.
set.expected: XNA documents LocalNetworkGamer.SendData as sending to all gamers in a session ('This includes the gamer sending the packet') without any session-type qualifier, and describes Local sessions as making it easier to share code between local and online modes; the decompiled SendDataWorker queues every packet regardless of session type. CNA's own LocalNetworkGamer.hpp repeats 'every gamer in the session', no CNA document lists the non-delivery as a limitation, and CNA's CLAUDE.md says XNA wins over FNA where they disagree.
set.actual: LocalNetworkGamer::SendData enqueues a PacketSend event; NetworkSession::Update in {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession.cpp}} delivers it only when ENetBackend::RealNetworkingEnabled(sessionType_) (true for SystemLink alone, {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ENetBackend.cpp|ENetBackend.cpp}}) or the session is a service-backed PlayerMatch/Ranked session, so in Local and LocalWithLeaderboards sessions the event is silently dropped, including a packet a local gamer sends to itself or to another local gamer. SendData reports nothing and IsDataAvailable stays false. The drop is deliberate FNA parity, pinned by LocalNetworkGamerTest.SendDataThenReceiveDataRoundtrip and NetworkSessionTypePolicyTest.SendDataStaysFullySyntheticForEverySyntheticType, a comment in Update now records the no-op on the premise that these sessions "have no remote gamers", which overlooks delivery between local gamers, and no CNA header documents it.

set.title: QualityOfService of PlayerMatch and Ranked search results is never measured
set.summary: QualityOfService of a PlayerMatch or Ranked search result is never measured: IsAvailable stays false and the round-trip and bandwidth fields stay 0, so online lobbies cannot sort sessions by connection quality.

set.title: SDL_RENDERER throws for any Texture2D mip level above 0, so mipmapped textures (including XNB textures with mip chains) cannot be uploaded there
set.summary: SDL_RENDERER's texture renderer throws std::runtime_error from UpdatePixelsLevel for level > 0 because SDL_Renderer textures have no mip chain; the XNB Texture2D reader uploads every level it reads.
set.actual: SdlTextureRenderer::UpdatePixelsLevel ({{src:modules/renderers/sdl-renderer/src/SdlRenderer.cpp|SdlRenderer.cpp}}) throws std::runtime_error for level != 0 (“does not support mip-level texture uploads ... Use Texture2D::SetData(level=0, ...) only”), by design: SDL_Renderer textures have no mip chain. The XNB reader ({{src:modules/content/src/Xnb/Texture2DContentTypeReader.cpp|Texture2DContentTypeReader.cpp}}) creates the texture with mipMap = levelCount > 1 and calls SetData(level, ...) for every level; Texture2D::SetData forwards level > 0 to the renderer, so a mipmapped XNB texture fails to load on SDL_RENDERER with a std::runtime_error rather than a NotSupportedException.

set.actual:
SDL 3.5.0, the revision CNA pins (86296ac8), still documents SDL_GPUMultisampleState::sample_mask and enable_mask as reserved (“must be set to 0” / “false”). Since c7f6c68e5 (CNA-DEMOS DC-R2, on the owner's decision) {{src:modules/renderers/sdl-gpu/src/SdlGpuRenderer.cpp|SdlGpuRenderer.cpp}} records the mask in ApplyBlendState and judges it for every queued draw in PushDrawOrder against the bound target: on a multisampled target a mask that keeps every sample draws as before, one that keeps none drops the draw (exact, since such a draw writes no colour, depth, stencil or occlusion sample), and any other throws System::NotSupportedException; a single-sample target ignores the mask, as in XNA. RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask (C CNA_RENDERER_FEATURE_MULTI_SAMPLE_MASK) reports Restricted there. FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver writes the mask into the same reserved field, where it has no effect, so the FNA3D renderer reports the feature Supported on its OpenGL driver only ({{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Fna3d/Fna3dRenderer.hpp|Fna3dRenderer.hpp}}, MultiSampleMaskSupportEXT); on the SDL_GPU driver a partial mask is ignored without an exception. EasyGL (where the context has glSampleMaski), WEBGPU, SOFTWARE and DIRECTX9 report and apply arbitrary masks.

Narrowed since first recorded: SDL_GPU no longer drops the mask silently: masks keeping every sample or none are applied exactly, a partial mask is refused by name, and the support is queryable. CNA records the boundary in {{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2.

set.blast_radius: MSAA techniques that rely on partial sample masks (alpha-to-coverage emulation, stippled transparency) on SDL_GPU, the default renderer on Windows, macOS and iOS, where they now throw, and on FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver, where the mask is ignored. set.title: EasyGL on GLES/WebGL contexts without GL_NV_polygon_mode or WEBGL_polygon_mode refuses most wireframe triangle draws
set.summary: Without a polygon-mode extension EasyGL draws only two bounded stock routes as line loops (non-indexed PositionColor and indexed PositionNormal TriangleLists); every other FillMode::WireFrame triangle draw throws NotSupportedException.
set.actual:
{{src:modules/renderers/easygl/src/EasyGLRenderer.cpp|EasyGLRenderer.cpp}}'s RequireSupportedFillModeEXT throws NotSupportedException for TriangleList/TriangleStrip draws when wireframe is requested and neither extension is present, with a message pointing at SupportsCapability(GraphicsCapability::WireFrame), unless the draw qualifies for one of two bounded stock routes that draw each triangle as a line loop. CanDrawStockWireframeAsLineLoops takes a single-stream, non-indexed VertexPositionColor TriangleList drawn with the stock effect, clipped in homogeneous space, with no culling, depth, stencil, scissor, bias, multisampling or render target. CanDrawStockIndexedWireframeAsLineLoops takes an indexed 24-byte VertexPositionNormal TriangleList with the stock lit program, keeping face culling and the depth test. TriangleStrip, other vertex layouts, custom, compiled, skinned or PBR effects, render targets, multisampling, scissor, stencil and depth bias still throw, and GraphicsCapability::WireFrame remains false.

Fixed since first recorded: the two line-loop routes (SAMPLE-048, 251bf6c98 and 96b5038de; SAMPLE-055, cefe6c83b).

set.summary: ES 3.0 and WebGL 2 only offer GL_ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED, so EasyGL reports whether any sample passed rather than how many; the public OcclusionQuery::isPixelCountPreciseEXT() reports which kind of count is in effect, but only after the first query has begun.
set.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/src/EasyGLRenderer.cpp|EasyGLRenderer.cpp}} resolves the precise target once per process (ResolvePreciseTarget, at the first EasyGLOcclusionQueryRenderer::Begin); where only GL_ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED exists, PixelCount is 0 or 1 and EasyGLOcclusionQueryRenderer::PixelCountIsPreciseEXT() (behind the public OcclusionQuery::isPixelCountPreciseEXT()) returns false. That accessor reads a process-wide flag that starts unresolved, so it returns false until some query has called Begin(), and it therefore also under-reports on desktop GL before first use.

set.summary: The SDL3 platform truncates every wheel event to whole notches before scaling by 120 (a deliberate FNA-parity rule in docs/input-fna-fidelity.md), so high-resolution wheels and touchpads can scroll without changing ScrollWheelValue; XNA accumulates 1/120 units.
set.expected: XNA 4.0 on Windows adds the raw signed WM_MOUSEWHEEL delta to the wheel value (MouseMessageHooker.WndProc, decompiled reference), so a high-resolution wheel moves it in steps smaller than 120. The SDL3 backend deliberately follows FNA instead (cast to int before multiplying by 120), which is the documented and tested behaviour; the contract on SDL3 is whole notches.
set.title: ScrollWheelValue drops sub-notch wheel motion: the SDL3 platform counts whole notches only, where XNA accumulates raw wheel units
set.actual:
{{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3EventMapper.cpp|Sdl3EventMapper.cpp}} passes SDL's float wheel.x/wheel.y, and AccumulateWheel in {{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3InputServices.cpp|Sdl3InputServices.cpp}} converts each event to an integer number of notches before multiplying by 120. An event of 0.25 notch adds nothing, so a touchpad or smooth-scrolling wheel that reports fractions per event can leave ScrollWheelValue unchanged for a whole gesture. SDL delivers the fractional amounts and CNA discards them, so this is a narrower contract on CNA's side, not a host constraint.

{{src:docs/input-fna-fidelity.md|input-fna-fidelity.md}} records the truncation as an intentional FNA match that keeps the value “a clean multiple of 120 exactly like XNA”; XNA's own hook does not truncate.

set.title: Threaded Emscripten builds on the default WasmFS have no persistent storage, so StorageDevice refuses rather than saving
set.summary: Threaded Emscripten builds default to WasmFS, which cannot link IDBFS, so StorageDevice there reports StorageDeviceNotConnectedException instead of persisting saves unless the application configures CNA_EMSCRIPTEN_USE_WASMFS=OFF.
set.public_contract: StorageDevice/StorageContainer and LocalGamerServicesStore in threaded Emscripten builds
set.actual: Since 8a67da536 and c5986156d the storage module links IDBFS. A pre-js hook ({{src:modules/storage/src/WebStoragePre.js|WebStoragePre.js}}) mounts /cna-storage and /save over IndexedDB with autoPersist and restores them before main(), and {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp|StorageDevice.cpp}} roots storage, and so the gamer-services store, there. {{src:modules/storage/CMakeLists.txt|CMakeLists.txt}} adds these link options only when NOT CNA_ENABLE_EMSCRIPTEN_THREADS OR NOT CNA_EMSCRIPTEN_USE_WASMFS. A threaded build on its default WasmFS therefore never sets Module.cnaStorageReady, and EnsureStorageRoot throws StorageDeviceNotConnectedException. A failed IndexedDB restore has the same result. Turning WasmFS off restores persistence, but {{src:docs/web-emscripten-graphics-limitations.md|the web limitations page}} warns that worker file access then waits on the browser thread.

set.summary: Under SDL3's Wayland video driver the desktop pointer position reads (0, 0) and the cursor cannot be warped reliably; on the web a gamepad appears only after the player presses a button on it, and relative mouse mode engages only after a click.
set.public_contract: Mouse::GetGlobalPositionEXT / WarpGlobalEXT on a Wayland session (SDL3's wayland video driver); GamePad connection and Mouse relative mode in Emscripten builds
set.actual: {{src:docs/platform-input-notes.md|platform-input-notes.md}} records, as verified in CNA's own input work (task 783), that under Wayland SDL_GetGlobalMouseState silently returns (0, 0) whatever the real cursor does, because the compositor does not give clients desktop coordinates, and that the operating-system cursor cannot be warped reliably. {{src:modules/platform/src/Sdl3/Sdl3InputServices.cpp|Sdl3Mouse}} passes those answers through: TryGetGlobalPosition reports success with SDL's values, and SetGlobalPosition returns SDL_WarpMouseGlobal's result. Window-local Mouse::SetPosition keeps XNA's contract through a virtual anchor. The same document records that the browser Gamepad API shows controllers only “until the user presses a button” and that pointer lock “requires a user gesture” and can be exited by the browser.

set.summary: On every Windows target CNA leaves Xml.Serialization out of its Sharp Runtime closure and drops both XmlSerializationEXTTests. The exclusion was added to avoid an unguarded <poll.h> in sharp-runtime's Diagnostics, which has since been fixed upstream; it no longer avoids that dependency, because CNA's closure already contains Xml, which depends on Diagnostics, so the surface is unavailable on Windows only because the build condition was left in place.
set.actual: When CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is Windows (MinGW cross builds and native MSVC), {{src:cmake/SharpRuntimeConsumption.cmake|SharpRuntimeConsumption.cmake}} does not append Xml.Serialization to CNA's Sharp Runtime closure, so SharpRuntime::Xml.Serialization does not exist, and {{src:cmake/UnitTests.cmake|UnitTests.cmake}} filters out the math and input XmlSerializationEXTTests.cpp. The stated cause is sharp-runtime's Diagnostics Process.cpp including <poll.h> outside its POSIX guard. In the local sharp-runtime checkout that include was moved inside the guard by commit 88c12f15 (2026-09-14), which sharp-runtime next @ 41b918c9 contains. The exclusion no longer avoids the problem: CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_DEFAULT_COMPONENTS names Xml on every platform with no Windows override, and sharp-runtime's Xml component has a private dependency on Diagnostics, so a Windows build compiles that file whether or not Xml.Serialization is selected (the Xml addition and the exclusion were made on different branches and first met in the 2026-09-11 merge). CNA's CMake pins no sharp-runtime revision, and the workflows that do pin one use revisions from 15 to 28 August 2026, all older than the fix. The exclusion is unconditional.

append.evidence: Independent re-verification: Checked by reading at 009d40f5, and the sharp-runtime fix and the Xml component's dependencies by reading the local sharp-runtime checkout (next @ 41b918c9, not pinned by the snapshot); not executed. The pinned CI revisions were compared with commit 88c12f15 by ancestry and none contains it. Not established: whether a Windows build with the component re-enabled compiles today.

The remaining terms (LookAt's rotation block, the perspective depth terms M33 and M43) are exercised only indirectly, by {{src:modules/graphics/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/ViewportTests.cpp|ViewportTests.cpp}} (projection and unprojection derived by hand), the bounding-frustum tests and graphics-ext consumers. set.actual: BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox in {{src:modules/math/src/BoundingSphere.cpp|BoundingSphere.cpp}} computes the centre as (Min + Max) / 2 and the radius as Distance(center, Max); XNA uses Vector3.Lerp(Min, Max, 0.5f) and Vector3.Distance(Min, Max) * 0.5f. {{src:modules/math/src/MathHelper.cpp|MathHelper.cpp}} evaluates Hermite and CatmullRom in double (Hermite with endpoint shortcuts for amounts within machine epsilon of 0 or 1) and SmoothStep through that Hermite, whereas XNA's MathHelper computes all three in float: Lerp(value1, value2, t*t*(3 - 2t)) for SmoothStep and its own float polynomials for Hermite and CatmullRom. The vector SmoothStep forms (SmoothStepScalar in {{src:modules/math/src/Vector2.cpp|Vector2.cpp}}, Vector3.cpp and Vector4.cpp) evaluate the float Hermite basis with zero tangents, where XNA computes value1 + (value2 - value1) * (t*t*(3 - 2t)). The vector Hermite forms (HermiteScalar) use the same float polynomial and operation order as XNA's Vector2/3/4.Hermite, so there only the evaluation precision of the 32-bit x87 runtime could differ. Agreement in the last bit is plausible for many inputs but unmeasured.

append.evidence: Independent re-verification: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. XNA formulas were compared with the decompiled XNA 4.0 MathHelper, Vector2, Vector3, Vector4 and BoundingSphere; the public contract should list the vector SmoothStep helpers rather than the vector Hermite helpers as the ones with different arithmetic. The numerical difference was not measured.

set.title: No test pins EffectParameter's divergences for CNA-constructed parameters, including a SetValue(Texture*) that GetValueTexture2D() does not read back
set.summary: Parameters without compiled storage keep separate base and typed texture slots and refuse numeric access only for Object-class parameters; the C API smoke test exercises the lenient string, numeric and texture setters, but no test pins that a texture set through the base overload reads back as null, or that the numeric refusal is by class rather than by storage.
set.actual: In {{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/EffectParameter.cpp|EffectParameter.cpp}}, RequireNumericParameter runs first in every numeric accessor and refuses only Object-class parameters, whether or not the parameter has compiled storage, so its comment's carve-out for CNA-constructed parameters is really a class rule: a CNA-constructed Object-class parameter still refuses numeric access. When compiledStorage_ is null nothing else is checked: SetValue(const std::string&) stores the string whatever the record's type, numeric setters write floatData_ whatever the class, and SetValue(Texture*) writes textureData_ while GetValueTexture2D() returns texture2DData_, so a texture set through the base-class overload reads back as null (the header records the separate texture slots as an out-of-scope API-shape decision, Task 863).

append.evidence: Independent re-verification: Checked by reading the named sources at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. Tests: EffectTests.cpp and {{src:tests/support/CNA/TestSupport/CompiledEffectConformance.hpp|CompiledEffectConformance.hpp}} cover compiled-mode checks; EffectParameterTests.cpp covers typed round trips only; {{src:modules/c-api/tests/pure_c/EffectParameterSmoke.c|EffectParameterSmoke.c}} (CApi_EffectParameterSmoke) sets a string, matrices, quaternions and textures on a standalone Vector/Single parameter but always sets the typed texture slot before reading it back, and no test asserts the Object-class numeric refusal or the base-overload read-back result.

• {{src:cmake/UnitTests.cmake|UnitTests.cmake}} removes those eight suites from CnaTests for every non-SDL3 audio selection, because they read SDL3_mixer's own track handles. set.title: Media paths without tests: the natural song end on SDL3_mixer, the failed visualization install and SavePicture's IOException
set.actual:
• Natural song end on SDL3_mixer. OnMusicTrackStopped sets the ended flag from the audio thread and Update advances, stops or repeats. The only test that lets a song finish, MediaPlayerTest.Mp3AndFlacSongsPlayThroughCnasOwnMixerToTheirEnd, is compiled only for ALSA audio.
  • Visualization without a tap. The comment on VisualizationEnabledStateStaysConsistentWithGetVisualizationData states that the suite always has a dummy SDL device, so the no-mixer and failed-install branches of setIsVisualizationEnabledProperty are correct by construction only.
  • SavePicture failure. MediaLibrary::SavePicture throws System::IO::IOException when the store returns no path. The store's name-sanitising and empty-root cases are tested at store level (SavedPictureStoreTests.cpp), but no test drives the public method into the exception.

Fixed since first recorded: MediaLibrary::Dispose now makes its properties and SavePicture throw ObjectDisposedException, as XNA does (45f704c04, CNA-DEMOS-ISSUE-098), with new MediaLibrary and collection tests.

set.title: The hand-written CnaPlatformTests filter misses TerminalPresenterThroughPlatformTest and nine other platform suites, so the platform CI cells never select them
set.summary: CnaPlatformTests selects suites by hand-written name tokens: TerminalPresenter.* misses TerminalPresenterThroughPlatformTest, and nine more platform suites (key codes, scancodes, filesystem, sensor session, SDL3 device services, input devices, system back, exit under lock) match no platform filter. Only four of their cases are selected, by the input filter's case-name tokens.
set.actual:
• The filter in {{src:cmake/UnitTests.cmake|UnitTests.cmake}} contains the token TerminalPresenter.*. A GoogleTest pattern matches the full Suite.Case name, and TerminalPresenter.* requires a literal dot after TerminalPresenter; the suite is named TerminalPresenterThroughPlatformTest in {{src:modules/platform/tests/CNA/Platform/TerminalPresenterTests.cpp|TerminalPresenterTests.cpp}} (a T, not a dot, follows), so it is not selected. It runs only as its own case through gtest_discover_tests(CnaTests) in an unfiltered ctest (the general-tests workflow), never in the terminal cell that filters to ^CnaPlatformTests$.
  • The same hand-written selection misses nine further suites of modules/platform/tests that no CnaPlatformTests or CnaPlatformWindowTests filter matches and no workflow names: KeyCodeTests, KeyCodeTableEquivalenceTests, ScancodeTests, StandardFileSystemTests, SensorSessionContractTests, Sdl3DeviceServicesTest, Sdl3InputDevicesTest, Sdl3SystemBackTest and Sdl3PlatformExitUnderLockTest. The input filter (CnaInputTests, ctest -L input) reaches only four of their cases through its case-name tokens: ScancodeTests.TheValuesAreHidKeyboardUsageIds and three Sdl3DeviceServicesTest haptic cases. Sdl3PlatformLinuxHintsTest, counted in an earlier version of this entry, is selected by the input filter's *Joystick* token and is not missed. Like the terminal case, the rest run only as discovered cases of an unfiltered ctest.

SDL_GPU cannot produce half rate through its API: it applies ordinary one-vblank vsync for Two and records the fallback (GetAppliedSwapIntervalEXT, pinned by sdlgpu_presentation_surface_test). A timing record would verify half rate only for the renderers that hand 2 to the driver, such as EasyGL and DIRECTX9 (D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_TWO).

set.title: CNA::Devices extension tests use canned platforms or check only that the host call does not fail, and exist only in a CNA_DEVICES=ON build
set.summary: Camera, FileDialog, MessageBox and SystemTray tests drive canned platform services; the Clipboard, DisplayInfo, Locale, PowerInfo, SystemInfo and UrlLauncher tests call the host but mostly assert only that nothing crashes; every body is wrapped in #ifdef CNA_DEVICES (default OFF), so only the devices workflow's ON build runs them.
set.expected: Each host-integration service has at least one test that fails when the real platform service misbehaves.
set.actual: CMakeLists.txt declares CNA_DEVICES OFF by default; the CNA::Devices sources and the test files under modules/devices-ext/tests (for example {{src:modules/devices-ext/tests/CNA/Devices/PowerInfoTests.cpp|PowerInfoTests.cpp}}) are wrapped in #ifdef CNA_DEVICES, so a default build compiles empty translation units, by design because the layer is opt-in, and devices-tests.yml builds the devices-ubsan preset with it ON. With the option on, CameraTests, FileDialogTest, MessageBoxTest and SystemTrayTests use canned platforms, which prove the wrappers' forwarding rather than SDL3 behaviour (CNA-VGAP-007). ClipboardTests, LocaleTests, PowerInfoTests and UrlLauncherTests call the host's real service but accept any outcome: does-not-crash, a valid enum, or a read-back checked only when the set succeeded; SystemInfoTests asserts positive core and RAM counts, and one DisplayInfo case creates a real hidden window. The workflow's hand-written suite filter also never selects the FileDialog and MessageBox suites (CNA-BUG-035).

append.evidence: Independent re-verification: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. Overlaps CNA-VGAP-007 (the SDL3 camera, tray and dialog-result paths), which is the platform half of the same gap.

CNA-BUG-084.evidence: XNA 4.0's fixed-step Tick applies forceElapsedTimeToZero to the measured elapsed time, but the flagged tick then finds num == 0 whole steps in the accumulator and returns before clock.AdvanceFrameTime(); GameClock.lastRealTime is therefore not advanced and the load's elapsed time reappears on the next tick, where the 500 ms clamp applies. XNA defers the catch-up burst by one tick (about 30 updates) instead of removing it; CNA runs it immediately (up to 29). The only residue is that XNA's ResetElapsedTime also clears the running-slowly counters, too small to stand as a defect. Deep Dive game-time-and-timestep.html#reset-elapsed-time corrected accordingly.

CNA-BUG-089.evidence: XNA 4.0's GraphicsDeviceManager.Dispose(bool) has no re-entrancy guard at all: it removes the service, disposes the device and raises Disposed last, so a Disposed handler that disposes the manager again recurses in XNA exactly as described. CNA's guard (set after the event) is at least as safe for sequential repeated Dispose calls, which CNA's regression test covers; the header states no re-entrancy contract. A robustness nit, not a contract violation.

CNA-BUG-136.evidence: The candidate described a deliberate, documented and tested choice as a defect. At TARGET the scancode path drops the two ISO-layout extra keys instead of mapping them to Keys::None (docs/input-fna-fidelity.md, accepted decisions INPUT-KBD-011 and INPUT-KBD-019, extending DEC-16), FNA itself maps them to Keys.None, VolumeMute has no desktop SDL source in FNA either, and Keyboard.hpp documents an empty scancode name for a key without a scancode. The drop is asserted by the test UnknownAndIsoExtraScancodesAreDropped in SdlInputBridgeKeyboardTests.cpp, so the candidate's statement that no test covers the ISO key was wrong. The input-model Deep Dive already states the consequence (OemBackslash and VolumeMute have no physical position and do not round-trip through the helpers). Only the platform's own keycode table knowing OemBackslash is a design difference, not a fault.

added.title: BoundingSphere(Vector3 center, float radius) accepts a negative radius, where XNA 4.0 throws ArgumentException
added.summary: CNA's BoundingSphere(Vector3, float) constructor stores any radius, while XNA 4.0's throws ArgumentException for radius < 0, so a negative radius is silently accepted.
added.public_contract: CNA::BoundingSphere::BoundingSphere(Vector3 center, float radius) (Microsoft::Xna::Framework::BoundingSphere)
added.expected: XNA 4.0's constructor (read from the decompiled genuine Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly, BoundingSphere.cs) is if (radius < 0f) throw new ArgumentException(FrameworkResources.NegativeRadius); followed by the two assignments, so a sphere with a negative radius cannot be constructed through it.
added.actual: BoundingSphere::BoundingSphere(Vector3, float) in {{src:modules/math/src/BoundingSphere.cpp|BoundingSphere.cpp}} is a bare initializer list, Center(center), Radius(radius): it validates nothing, so a caller that passes a negative radius gets a sphere with a negative Radius instead of the exception. Sibling math code already throws sharp-runtime exceptions for invalid arguments (System::ArgumentException in BoundingBox.cpp), so the mechanism exists.

sources.note: BoundingSphere::BoundingSphere(Vector3, float): an unvalidated initializer list
the constructor declaration
ConstructorStoresCenterAndRadius: positive radius only

added.evidence: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; nothing was built or executed for this entry. XNA's guard was read in the decompiled reference (xna4-decomp). Found by the independent adversarial review of the math entries, not by an earlier audit; no published entry covers it (CNA-BUG-070 is about Contains, CNA-BUG-025 about the PlaneIntersectionType Doxygen). The other construction paths of the type (default constructor, the CreateFrom* helpers, Transform) were not examined for the same invariant.
added.tests_current: BoundingSphereTests.cpp constructs spheres with a positive radius (ConstructorStoresCenterAndRadius); no case passes a negative one.
added.regression_test: A test that BoundingSphere(Vector3::Zero, -1.0f) throws an ArgumentException-family exception, and that a zero radius still constructs.
added.blast_radius: Code that builds a BoundingSphere from a computed radius, and XNA code that relies on the constructor's ArgumentException to reject bad input. Correct programs that only pass non-negative radii are unaffected.
added.workaround: Validate the radius (radius >= 0) before constructing.

added.title: Vector3, Vector4, Quaternion and Matrix GetHashCode add raw int bit patterns with signed arithmetic, which overflows (undefined behaviour) for ordinary values
added.summary: The four GetHashCode functions sum FloatHash results as int with plain +; three 1.0f components already exceed INT_MAX, so the sum is signed-overflow undefined behaviour, while Vector2::GetHashCode already sums as unsigned to avoid it.
added.public_contract: CNA::Vector3::GetHashCode, Vector4::GetHashCode, Quaternion::GetHashCode and Matrix::GetHashCode (Microsoft::Xna::Framework)
added.expected: Signed integer overflow is undefined behaviour in C++, so a hash that sums the int bit patterns of several floats must wrap through unsigned arithmetic. Vector2::GetHashCode does exactly that, and its comment says why (“Unsigned wraparound avoids signed-overflow UB (UBSan, INPUT-BUILD-006); result unchanged”). .NET's unchecked int addition wraps, which is the behaviour XNA's hashes rely on.
added.actual: FloatHash returns the IEEE bit pattern of the float as an int. Vector3::GetHashCode in {{src:modules/math/src/Vector3.cpp|Vector3.cpp}} returns FloatHash(X) + FloatHash(Y) + FloatHash(Z) with int operands; 1.0f is 0x3F800000 = 1,065,353,216, so Vector3(1, 1, 1) sums to 3,196,059,648 and overflows a 32-bit int. Vector4 (four terms), Quaternion (four) and Matrix (sixteen) do the same. In practice the sum usually wraps, but it is undefined behaviour: a UBSan signed-integer-overflow run reports it, and an optimiser may assume it cannot happen. Vector2 was already repaired; these four were not.

added.title: EasyGL family: ClearColorAndStencil leaves the stencil write mask forced to all ones, so a later draw ignores StencilWriteMask
added.summary: GraphicsDevice::Clear with Target and Stencil reaches EasyGLRenderer::ClearColorAndStencil, which forces the GL stencil mask open and never restores it, unlike the other EasyGL clears (REMED-GFX-237). A later StencilWriteMask-limited draw is not limited.
added.expected: XNA's Clear ignores StencilWriteMask but does not change the device's DepthStencilState, so a draw after the clear obeys the state the game assigned. EasyGL's own rule (REMED-GFX-237, stated in EasyGLRenderer.hpp and in OpenGL4Renderer.cpp) is that every clear puts back the write masks it forced open, because a game need not reassign its DepthStencilState before the next draw.
added.actual: EasyGLRenderer::ClearColorAndDepth, ClearDepth, ClearStencil, ClearDepthAndStencil and ClearColorDepthAndStencil all call RestoreWriteMasksAfterClear. ClearColorAndStencil sets the stencil mask to all ones, clears, and restores only the colour mask and the scissor. After GraphicsDevice::Clear(ClearOptions::Target | ClearOptions::Stencil, ...) the GL stencil write mask stays 0xFFFFFFFF until ApplyDepthStencilState runs again, so a later draw can write stencil bits its StencilWriteMask forbids until the depth/stencil state is applied again. OpenGL4Renderer::ClearColorAndStencil carries a comment that EasyGL's twin of this route does not put the mask back. The restore check in easygl_graphicsdevice_clear_stencil_test.cpp (Check D) uses ClearOptions::Stencil only.

added.title: PORTABLEGL depth clears force glDepthMask(GL_TRUE) and never restore it, although their own comment says both masks are restored as EasyGL does
added.summary: ClearColorAndDepth, ClearDepth, ClearDepthAndStencil and ClearColorDepthAndStencil call glDepthMask(GL_TRUE) and never put the depth write mask back; only the colour mask is restored.
added.public_contract: GraphicsDevice::Clear with a depth option on the PORTABLEGL renderer (PortableGLRenderer::ClearColorAndDepth, ClearDepth, ClearDepthAndStencil, ClearColorDepthAndStencil)
added.expected: The comment in ClearColorAndDepth states the rule: XNA's Clear ignores DepthBufferWriteEnable and ColorWriteChannels, so both masks are “neutralized here and restored afterwards, exactly as EasyGL does”. EasyGL implements the restore with RestoreWriteMasksAfterClear (REMED-GFX-237: “restores the write masks a clear had to force open”), so a clear never changes what a later draw's depth/stencil state says.
added.actual: In {{src:modules/renderers/portablegl/src/PortableGLRenderer.cpp|PortableGLRenderer.cpp}} the four clears that touch depth call glDepthMask(GL_TRUE) before glClear. Only the colour mask is put back afterwards (from colorWriteChannels); the depth write mask is left GL_TRUE until ApplyDepthStencilState next runs glDepthMask(depthWriteEnable ? GL_TRUE : GL_FALSE). A later draw through a state with DepthBufferWriteEnable false can therefore write depth after such a clear, if the state has not been re-applied in between.

added.expected: XNA 4.0's ReceiveData(byte[] data, int offset, out NetworkGamer sender) (read from the decompiled genuine Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net assembly) peeks at the next packet and, when offset + packet.Size > data.Length, throws ArgumentException(PacketArrayTooSmall) before it dequeues, so a caller that supplied too small a buffer keeps the packet and learns the size it needs. Only then does it dequeue and copy.
added.actual: {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/LocalNetworkGamer.cpp|LocalNetworkGamer::ReceiveData}} moves the front packet out of packetQueue_ and pops it first, then computes len = min(packet size, data.size()). A packet larger than the buffer is therefore consumed and truncated to the buffer size, and the call returns without an error; the exception path only fires when offset is negative or offset + len exceeds the buffer. A comment in the function records that the ordering “match[es] FNA's Dequeue()-before-Array.Copy”: it is a deliberate port of FNA, whereas CNA's rule is that XNA wins where the two disagree.

added.title: Matrix::Decompose follows FNA's algorithm, not XNA 4.0's: a mirrored matrix decomposes to positive scales and a non-unit quaternion, and a sheared matrix reports success
added.summary: Matrix::Decompose never checks the determinant: a mirrored matrix returns positive scales, a non-unit quaternion and true where XNA 4.0 negates the largest scale, and a sheared matrix returns true where XNA returns false.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Matrix::Decompose(Vector3& scale, Quaternion& rotation, Vector3& translation)
added.expected: XNA 4.0's Matrix.Decompose (read from the decompiled genuine Microsoft.Xna.Framework assembly and its IL; not executed) takes each scale as the length of the row, orders the three axes by scale, substitutes a canonical basis row for any axis shorter than 0.0001 and normalises the rows. When the determinant of that basis is negative it negates the largest axis's scale and row, so Matrix::CreateScale(-1, 1, 1) decomposes to scale (-1, 1, 1), the identity rotation and true. When the squared error of the determinant from 1 exceeds 0.0001, as for a sheared matrix, it returns false with an identity rotation. CNA's own rule is that XNA 4.0 wins where FNA and XNA disagree.
added.actual: {{src:modules/math/src/Matrix.cpp|Matrix::Decompose}} is the FNA (and MonoGame) algorithm: each scale takes its sign from the product of the row's first four elements, which is always +1 for an affine matrix because M14, M24 and M34 are zero; it divides each row by its scale and passes the result to Quaternion::CreateFromRotationMatrix. It never looks at the determinant and returns false only when a scale is within FLT_EPSILON of zero. CreateScale(-1, 1, 1) therefore yields scale (1, 1, 1), the non-unit quaternion (0, 0, 0, 0.7071) and true (a reflection has no rotation, so the trace-based conversion returns a quaternion of norm 0.7071), and a sheared matrix returns true with a quaternion that is not a unit rotation. MatrixTest.DecomposeReportsPositiveScaleForAMirroredAffineTransform pins the FNA result and attributes it to XNA's “per-row sign heuristic”, which the XNA IL does not contain.

added.title: NetworkSession's Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink Begin/End pairs are synchronous: Begin runs the callback and returns a completed result, and End does the work on the caller's thread
added.summary: For Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink sessions, BeginCreate, BeginFind and BeginJoin run the callback inline and return a completed result; End* then blocks: 150 ms for a SystemLink Find, up to 5 s for a SystemLink Join.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession::BeginCreate/BeginFind/BeginJoin and the matching End* methods for Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink sessions
added.expected: XNA 4.0 (read from the decompiled Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net assembly and its async dispatcher; not executed) registers each Begin* operation as pending: IsCompleted stays false until a dispatcher thread finishes it, the wait handle is signalled then, the AsyncCallback is queued to the thread pool, and End* returns the finished result.
added.actual: In {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession.cpp}} a NetworkSessionAction starts complete (IsCompleted true, wait handle signalled, CompletedSynchronously true). For every session type except PlayerMatch and Ranked, BeginCreate, BeginFind and BeginJoin invoke the AsyncCallback inline (InvokeActiveActionCallback) before returning. The work then runs in End* on the caller's thread. On native builds, EndFind waits the fixed 150 ms SystemLink discovery window, and EndJoin pumps the joined session for up to 5 s until the host's welcome arrives. A game that polls IsCompleted every frame and calls End* when it turns true therefore stalls there. Service-backed PlayerMatch/Ranked Create, Find and Join, and BeginJoinInvited, are genuinely pending (QueueOnlineSession, QueueServiceSearch): IsCompleted stays false until the CNA service answers, so they are not part of this entry.

added.title: Only EasyGL leases its context to other threads: on every other renderer, graphics resources created on a loading thread have no CNA-level exclusion against the frame
added.summary: GraphicsDevice's resource registry is now locked and EasyGL leases its context to resource creation on any thread, but every other renderer returns no lease and has no synchronization of its own, while XNA 4.0 creates its device D3DCREATE_MULTITHREADED.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::GraphicsDevice and GraphicsResource: creating or disposing resources from a thread other than the game thread
added.expected: XNA 4.0 creates its Direct3D 9 device with D3DCREATE_MULTITHREADED (decompiled GraphicsDevice.CreateDevice sets creation flags 38, which is 0x26 and includes 0x4), so a loading thread can create textures and buffers while the game thread runs, and the game thread may wait for that thread. {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/RendererThreadContextLease.hpp|RendererThreadContextLease.hpp}} says renderer families that return no lease 'support concurrent resource creation directly or own a different synchronization boundary'.
added.actual:
GraphicsDevice's resource registry is locked: AddResourceReference, RemoveResourceReference and TransferResourceReference take resourcesMutex_ ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp|GraphicsDevice.cpp}}, KF-1a). On EasyGL, resource construction, SetData, GetData and Dispose of textures, render targets, vertex and index buffers take the renderer's context lease on whatever thread they run ({{src:modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsResource.cpp|GraphicsResource.cpp}}, LeaseRendererContext, KF-1), ContentReader holds it for a whole asset, and the game thread holds it for Initialize, BeginRun, every Tick and EndRun ({{src:modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp|Game.cpp}}, AcquireGameThreadContextLease, KF-16), so a loading thread works between frames. Only EasyGLRenderer implements AcquireThreadContextLeaseEXT; SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, DIRECTX9, FNA3D and SOFTWARE return no lease, and their sources hold no lock for it (SDL_GPU's only mutexes guard its queued buffer uploads and its shader-cross session). The lease contract nevertheless still claims that lease-less renderers 'support concurrent resource creation directly or own a different synchronization boundary'. On EasyGL itself, a game thread that waits inside LoadContent, Update or Draw for a thread that is creating graphics resources deadlocks, because it still holds the context ({{src:docs/opengl33-renderer.md|opengl33-renderer.md}}); XNA 4.0 allows that wait.

Fixed since first recorded: the registry lock (KF-1a) and the EasyGL lease on resource construction, data transfer and disposal (KF-1, 00b9c9898) and on the whole frame (KF-16, a033a9184); native device construction and teardown are serialized (BINDFIX-050, 5b4edd6cc).

added.title: Vulkan passes XNA's normalised RasterizerState.DepthBias to vkCmdSetDepthBias unscaled, so a realistic bias has no effect
added.summary: VulkanRenderer hands DepthBias to vkCmdSetDepthBias raw, but that constant factor counts minimum depth steps; EasyGL, SDL_GPU, Metal and Direct3D 11 scale XNA's normalised value by the depth format, so -0.0001 offsets nothing on Vulkan.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Graphics::RasterizerState::DepthBias and SlopeScaleDepthBias on the VULKAN renderer (VulkanRenderer::ApplyRasterizerState)
added.expected: XNA 4.0 is Direct3D 9, where DepthBias is a normalised depth value added to the depth. CNA's renderer contract says so indirectly: {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp|IGraphicsRenderer.hpp}} documents in IRenderTargetRenderer::DepthBufferBitsEXT that an API whose bias is a multiple of the smallest resolvable depth step, naming Vulkan's depthBiasConstantFactor, needs the depth width to convert. FNA3D multiplies the XNA value by 65,535 (16-bit depth) or 16,777,215 (24-bit), and CNA's EasyGL, SDL_GPU, Metal and Direct3D 11 renderers convert it as well, so a sample that lifts a flat shadow with DepthBias = -0.0001f lifts it on each of them.
added.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/vulkan/src/VulkanRenderer.cpp|VulkanRenderer::ApplyRasterizerState}} stores DepthBias and SlopeScaleDepthBias as given, and the draw replay calls vkCmdSetDepthBias(cb, draw.depthBias, 0.0f, draw.slopeScaleDepthBias) with no depth-format scale; no Vulkan render-target class overrides DepthBufferBitsEXT. A constant factor of -0.0001 is about 1e-4 of one depth step, that is, no bias. {{src:modules/renderers/vulkan/examples/vulkan_depth_bias_test.cpp|vulkan_depth_bias_test.cpp}} uses -1e6 and -2e3 on purpose (“bias magnitudes are deliberately large”) and so cannot see the defect, and CNA's records close the failing Vulkan_DepthBias case as a test defect (VULKAN-091) without examining the product behaviour. The source comment that says the mapping matches FNA omits the scale. EasyGL's {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/EasyGL/EasyGLRenderer.hpp|EasyGLDepthBiasToPolygonOffsetUnits}} carries the 16/24-bit depth-format scale Vulkan lacks.

added.title: SignedInGamer::SignedIn does not replay already signed-in gamers to a late subscriber, unlike XNA 4.0
added.summary: XNA 4.0 raises SignedIn during Update and its add accessor replays each already signed-in gamer to a new handler; CNA raises it inside Initialize on a plain event, so a handler added afterwards never hears about the four stub gamers.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::GamerServices::SignedInGamer::SignedIn (event) and GamerServicesDispatcher::Initialize/Update
added.expected: In the genuine XNA 4.0 GamerServices assembly (read from its decompiled IL), sign-in changes are raised from GamerServicesDispatcher.Update, and SignedInGamer.SignedIn has a custom add accessor: after combining the delegate it loops over Gamer.SignedInGamers and invokes the newly added handler once for every gamer already signed in. The XNA documentation likewise says the event is raised during calls to Update. A game can therefore subscribe at any time and still learn who is signed in. CNA already reproduces such a replay for NetworkSession::GamerJoined, through an EventHandler replay hook, and {{src:docs/c-api/NET.md|NET.md}} documents that behaviour.
added.actual: SignedInGamer::SignedIn in SignedInGamer.cpp is a plain System::EventHandler with no replay hook, and GamerServicesDispatcher::Update is empty. Initialize raises OnSignIn once for each of its four stub gamers, synchronously inside the call, and a handler added afterwards is never called for them; the game must read Gamer::getSignedInGamersProperty() instead. The CNA presence demo subscribes 'before Initialize() runs so every SignedIn firing during startup is observed', and the C route cna_signed_in_gamer_subscribe_signed_in_ext adds its handler the same way. SignedOut is never raised in production, because OnSignOut has no caller outside SignedInGamerTestAccess. SignedInGamerTest.SignedInEventFires raises the event only after subscribing, so no test pins late-subscriber behaviour.

added.title: A join beyond MaxGamers is not refused: the host sends ServerWelcome, AddRemoteGamer throws Session is full!, and the receive path's catch-all drops it, so the joiner never sees SessionFull
added.summary: HandleClientHello sends ServerWelcome and registers wire ids before AddRemoteGamer checks capacity; the receive path swallows the exception, so an over-capacity client stays connected and NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull is never produced.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession::Join on a full host (ENetBackend HandleClientHello, NetworkSession::AddRemoteGamer, NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull)
added.expected: A client that joins a session already holding MaxGamers gamers should be refused with a NetworkSessionJoinException carrying NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull, the value the XNA API defines for exactly this case, and the host's roster and the other peers should be left alone.
added.actual: {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ENetBackend.cpp|HandleClientHello}} rejects only a duplicate handshake and a join in progress that the host forbids. It then creates the joining client's NetworkGamer objects, assigns and registers their wire ids, sends ServerWelcome, and only afterwards calls {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession::AddRemoteGamer}}, which throws InvalidOperationException(“Session is full!”) once allGamers_ has reached maxGamers_. The receive path wraps the whole message switch in a catch-all that drops the exception, so a bad packet cannot take down Update(). The over-capacity client therefore has been welcomed and stays connected with its wire ids registered, the gamers beyond the limit are never added to the host's roster or announced to the other peers, and the SystemLink path produces no SessionFull (only the online service binding, {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/OnlineSessionBinding.cpp|OnlineSessionBinding.cpp}}, throws it).

added.title: A NetworkSession BeginCreate, BeginFind or BeginJoin callback that calls the matching End* frees the action and the closure that is executing, and Begin* returns the freed pointer
added.summary: InvokeActiveActionCallback runs the AsyncCallback inline from BeginCreate, BeginFind and BeginJoin; the matching End* deletes the action, including the std::function that is executing, so captures read after End* and the IAsyncResult* that Begin* then returns point at freed memory. BeginJoinInvited always refuses and never invokes a callback.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession::BeginCreate/BeginFind/BeginJoin/BeginJoinInvited with a callback that calls the matching End*
added.expected: XNA's asynchronous pattern lets the AsyncCallback call the matching End* method to obtain the result, and the IAsyncResult that Begin* returned stays valid until the game drops it.
added.actual: {{src:modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp|NetworkSession.cpp}} calls action->Callback(*action) from inside BeginCreate, BeginFind and BeginJoin (through InvokeActiveActionCallback). EndFind deletes activeAction_ first thing, EndJoin right after copying the fields it needs, and EndCreate as soon as the session exists (or in its catch path). The action owns the const std::function Callback that is running, so a callback that calls the matching End* destroys its own closure: captures read after End* returns live in freed storage, and the IAsyncResult& it was given dangles. The function also returns the pointer it saved before invoking, so Begin* hands the caller an IAsyncResult* that is already freed, and a later IsCompleted call on it is a use after free. BeginJoinInvited (both overloads) throws GamerServicesNotAvailableException before it creates an action and EndJoinInvited throws ArgumentException, so that pair is not affected. The source comment treats the re-entrant case only as a stale-null problem and fixes that by saving the pointer first. CNA's own test NetworkSessionTest.BeginCreateCallbackCanReentrantlyCallEndCreate uses exactly this idiom (its callback assigns through a by-reference capture after EndCreate returns).

sources.note: InvokeActiveActionCallback and the delete activeAction_ at the top of EndCreate, EndFind, EndJoin and EndJoinInvited

added.evidence: Read at 009d40f5; nothing was executed, so the hazard is derived from the code: the undefined behaviour needs a callback that touches its captures or the returned result after calling End*, which is the idiomatic shape of XNA's asynchronous samples. Found by the C10 conservation reviewer (unit ch51) and re-verified by the orchestrator against InvokeActiveActionCallback and EndFind. It is distinct from {{issue:NEW-AUDIT-14}} (the Begin/End pairs are synchronous by design). NetworkSessionTest.BeginCreateCallbackCanReentrantlyCallEndCreate covers the path but passes in an ordinary build, because the freed memory is still intact when the callback reads its capture.
added.tests_current: NetworkSessionTests.BeginCreateInvokesCallbackExactlyOnceWithCorrectIdentity pins the inline callback, and NetworkSessionTest.BeginCreateCallbackCanReentrantlyCallEndCreate calls EndCreate from inside it and writes through a by-reference capture afterwards, so the idiom is exercised; nothing checks for the use of freed memory.
added.regression_test: Call BeginFind with a callback that calls EndFind and then reads a captured variable, under AddressSanitizer, and check the pointer returned by Begin*; the fix is to defer the deletion until the callback has returned.
added.blast_radius: Games that follow XNA's asynchronous pattern and call End* from the callback of a NetworkSession Begin/End pair (create, find, join): a read of a capture after End*, or any use of the returned result, is a use after free. Callbacks whose last action is End* and that keep no result are much less exposed.
added.workaround: Do not call End* from inside the callback: keep the IAsyncResult that the callback receives and call End* from the game loop after Begin* has returned, and do not use the pointer that Begin* returns.

added.title: SoundEffect::Play(volume, pitch, pan) clamps pitch, does not check volume and returns false when disposed, where XNA 4.0 throws
added.summary: XNA 4.0's SoundEffect.Play(float, float, float) throws ObjectDisposedException when disposed and ArgumentOutOfRangeException for volume or pitch out of range; CNA returns false when disposed, clamps pitch and passes volume through.
added.public_contract: SoundEffect::Play(float volume, float pitch, float pan) and the C route cna_sound_effect_play_with_settings
added.expected: XNA 4.0's SoundEffect.Play(float, float, float) (decompiled Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Audio.SoundEffect; read, not executed) throws ObjectDisposedException when the effect is disposed and assigns the arguments through the SoundEffectInstance Volume, Pitch and Pan setters, which throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException outside [0, 1], [-1, 1] and [-1, 1]. CNA's own SoundEffectInstance setters follow those ranges since KF-12 (49119a34c).
added.actual: SoundEffect::Play(float, float, float) in {{src:modules/audio/src/Xna/SoundEffect.cpp|SoundEffect.cpp}} returns false for a disposed effect, range-checks only pan, clamps pitch to [-1, 1] (its comment: "Pitch is clamped rather than validated") and hands volume to the mixer track's gain without a check. So Play(1.0f, 5.0f, 0.0f) plays where XNA throws, a volume of 2 or -1 is accepted, and a call on a disposed effect is refused silently instead of raising. The same values on a SoundEffectInstance throw, so the two paths disagree. {{src:modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/audio.h|audio.h}} documents the C route cna_sound_effect_play_with_settings with the same asymmetry ("pan is range-checked and pitch is clamped").

added.title: SendDataOptions cannot express XNA's combined Chat flags, and chat packets are always sent reliably
added.summary: XNA's SendDataOptions is a [Flags] enum whose Chat flag combines with Reliable and InOrder (values 5 to 7); CNA's is a plain enum 0 to 4 without bitwise operators, and the packet codec sends Chat, and any other value, reliably.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::SendDataOptions and LocalNetworkGamer::SendData(..., SendDataOptions)
added.expected: XNA 4.0 declares SendDataOptions as [Flags] (decompiled Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net; read, not executed): None 0, Reliable 1, InOrder 2, ReliableInOrder 3 and Chat 4, and documents that Chat "can be combined with either or both of the Reliable and InOrder flags", with ordered chat packets ordered relative to other chat packets only.
added.actual: {{src:modules/net/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Net/SendDataOptions.hpp|SendDataOptions.hpp}} declares a plain enum class with values 0 to 4 and no bitwise operators (its comment follows FNA, whose members are sequential), so SendDataOptions::Chat | SendDataOptions::Reliable does not compile and a combined value can only be produced by a cast. NetPacketCodec::SendDataOptionsToEnetFlags ({{src:modules/net/src/Internal/NetPacketCodec.cpp|NetPacketCodec.cpp}}) maps Reliable, ReliableInOrder and Chat, and any value outside the switch, to ENET_PACKET_FLAG_RELIABLE: chat packets are always reliable, and there is no separately ordered chat stream. CNA's own audit records the difference as GS-AUDIT-016 ({{src:audit/gamer-services/gamer-services-issues.md|gamer-services-issues.md}}).

added.origin: new finding at the c1c316b9 pin move: Apple campaign tasks AM4-034, AM4-099, AM4-191 and AM4-296 in the b0e97bb1..c1c316b9 delta
added.title: On Apple, SamplerState.MipMapLevelOfDetailBias does not reach the GPU on FNA3D's non-OpenGL drivers
added.summary: FNA3D on macOS and iOS hands a sampler LOD bias to SDL's Metal-backed GPU driver, which ignores it, so the bias is accepted without effect; RendererFeature::SamplerLevelOfDetailBias reports that.
added.public_contract: SamplerState.MipMapLevelOfDetailBias on the FNA3D renderer on macOS and iOS; GraphicsDevice::SupportsRendererFeatureEXT(RendererFeature::SamplerLevelOfDetailBias)
added.expected: XNA 4.0 applies SamplerState.MipMapLevelOfDetailBias on every device: a bias of +1 selects the next smaller mip level, and a game that sharpens or blurs textures with it gets the same mip selection everywhere.
added.actual:
FNA3D selects its SDL_GPU driver on Apple, which runs on SDL's Metal driver; that driver ignores mip_lod_bias, and FNA3D's MojoShader shaders have no other route for it, so the bias is accepted and has no effect. Fna3dRenderer::SamplerLodBiasReachesTheGpuEXT() ({{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dRenderer.cpp|Fna3dRenderer.cpp}}, AM4-191) reports false on Apple for every driver but OpenGL; nothing is thrown.

Since c6dec91fb (CNA-DEMOS-ISSUE-006) the answer is public: RendererFeature::SamplerLevelOfDetailBias, answered by Fna3dRenderer::AppliesSamplerLevelOfDetailBiasEXT() from the same probe, is false there, and CrossRendererContractTest.SamplerLevelOfDetailBiasSupportMatchesWhatSpriteBatchSamples requires each compiled-in renderer's answer to match the pixels. CNA closed ISSUE-006 on a complete checkpoint (6c8b042c4, 2026-10-24). CNA's own SDL_GPU renderer is not affected for SpriteBatch, the stock effects and compiled XNA effects, which carry the bias in their shaders (SDLGPU-121/122).

added.origin: new finding at the c1c316b9 pin move: AM4-189 made FNA3D's OcclusionQuery capability follow its driver
added.title: FNA3D has no occlusion queries on its SDL_GPU driver, the driver FNA3D tries first and the one it runs on Apple
added.summary: Fna3dRenderer probes queries only on FNA3D's OpenGL and Direct3D 11 drivers; on its SDL_GPU driver (FNA3D's first choice, and its Metal route on Apple) OcclusionQuery is reported unsupported and its constructor refuses, because SDL3's GPU API has no queries.
added.public_contract: OcclusionQuery and GraphicsCapability::OcclusionQuery on the FNA3D renderer
added.expected: XNA 4.0 offers OcclusionQuery on every HiDef device. Where a backend cannot count samples, CNA's rule is to say so: the capability answers false and the constructor refuses by name rather than returning a fabricated count.
added.actual: FNA3D chooses its driver at run time: its SDL_GPU driver first, then its Direct3D 11 driver, then its OpenGL driver ({{src:docs/fna3d-renderer.md|fna3d-renderer.md}}). At device creation Fna3dRenderer ({{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dRenderer.cpp|Fna3dRenderer.cpp}}) probes query support with FNA3D_CreateQuery only when the chosen driver is not SDL_GPU; on the SDL_GPU driver supportsOcclusionQueries_ stays false, SupportsCapability(OcclusionQuery) answers false and Fna3dRenderer::CreateOcclusionQuery ({{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dResources.cpp|Fna3dResources.cpp}}) returns no renderer, so the public OcclusionQuery constructor refuses with NotSupportedException. SDL3's GPU API has no occlusion-query commands (the same reason CNA's own SDL_GPU renderer refuses them). On Apple FNA3D runs that driver on Metal, so FNA3D has no occlusion queries there; elsewhere it has none unless FNA3D falls back to, or is pinned (FNA3D_FORCE_DRIVER) to, OpenGL or Direct3D 11.

added.origin: new finding at the c1c316b9 pin move: AM4-044 (14f74e81f) and AM4-123 (a1c0c4d91) make the relay refuse a libcurl without WebSockets by name, and CNA's Apple qualification records the macOS system libcurl as lacking it (owner decision in plans/plan_apple_m4.md AM4-044)
added.title: Online PlayerMatch and Ranked session traffic needs a libcurl with WebSocket support; with macOS's system libcurl the relay refuses with RELAY_SECURE_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE
added.summary: PlayerMatch and Ranked sessions carry their traffic over a WSS relay through libcurl's WebSocket API, so a libcurl without ws/wss and TLS (Apple's system libcurl 8.7.1, or one older than 7.86) refuses the relay and those sessions cannot run.
added.public_contract: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Net::NetworkSession Create, Join and JoinInvited for NetworkSessionType::PlayerMatch and Ranked with a configured CNA gamer-services endpoint; the realtime relay at /cna/relay/v1 and the push channel /cna/v1/events
added.expected: Once a CNA gamer-services endpoint is configured, online PlayerMatch and Ranked sessions work on every desktop host CNA builds for, as they do on Linux.
added.actual: Online session traffic (game data, voice, readiness) travels between machines through the service's authenticated WSS datagram relay, which CNA reaches through libcurl's WebSocket API (curl_ws_send/curl_ws_recv). Before it authenticates, {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/RelayWebSocket.cpp|RelayWebSocket.cpp}} checks the linked libcurl with relayTransportRefusal(): relayTransportRefusalFor refuses with RELAY_SECURE_WEBSOCKET_UNAVAILABLE unless the version is at least 7.86.0, its protocol list offers both ws and wss, and it has a TLS backend. Apple's system libcurl 8.7.1, which a macOS build links unless another curl is found, has no WebSocket support, so on such a build the relay never connects; the online session cannot become ready and, by reading {{src:modules/net/src/Internal/ServiceENetSession.cpp|ServiceENetSession.cpp}}, ends with a relay failure once its 15-second relay-recovery window has passed. The account's push channel (/cna/v1/events) uses the same libcurl WebSocket API in {{src:modules/gamer-services/src/Internal/GamerServicesBackend.cpp|GamerServicesBackend.cpp}}; without it the hints never arrive and the client falls back to its ordinary polling (invitations and parties every 5 seconds, messages and friends every 15). Sign-in, profiles, achievements, leaderboards, the session directory and SystemLink sessions do not use WebSockets and are unaffected. Before 14f74e81f the same build reported a misleading RELAY_CONFIGURATION instead of this refusal.

CNA's own record states the platform consequence: {{src:plans/plan_apple_m4.md|plan_apple_m4.md}} AM4-044 records the owner decision that with the system libcurl the relay cannot work on macOS and that Homebrew curl 8.22 has ws/wss, and {{src:docs/apple-platforms.md|apple-platforms.md}} records that a CNA build linking the SDK's libcurl 8.7.1 refuses the relay transport by name, so the server's harness-driven tests on the Mac needed a tree that found Homebrew curl. added.blast_radius: Games that use online PlayerMatch or Ranked sessions (and their voice) in builds linked against a libcurl without WebSocket support, notably macOS builds that link the system libcurl; push hints in such builds degrade to polling. Local, LocalWithLeaderboards and SystemLink sessions and the non-realtime gamer services are unaffected. iOS builds currently disable networking altogether, and an Android build without a target libcurl refuses the service as a browser does (CNA records both separately).
added.workaround: Build against a libcurl that offers ws and wss with TLS, for example Homebrew curl on macOS, so that CMake finds it before the system library.

added.summary: Since the native Windows and Apple renderers were retired, a build for Windows, macOS or iOS defaults to SDL_GPU, yet CNA records no native Windows run of it, no Apple run since the retirement and no iOS build.
added.public_contract: The per-host default renderer (CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER left unset) on Windows, macOS and iOS: SDL_GPU, through SDL's Direct3D 12 and Metal drivers
added.expected: A renderer that a build selects by default on a host has recorded evidence on that host: at least one native run of its suite, or of a named qualification set, on the driver SDL uses there.
added.actual: {{src:cmake/RendererIdentityDefault.cmake|RendererIdentityDefault.cmake}} sets the default to SDL_GPU when CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is Windows, Darwin or iOS. CNA's own handoff ({{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}}, section 5.2) records that SDL_GPU “is the default renderer on Windows, macOS and iOS but is not qualified there”: the evidence that exists is a full-tree pass with SDL's Metal driver on a Mac mini M4 during the AM4 campaign, before the retirement, and Wine runs of SDL's Direct3D 12 driver through vkd3d-proton; not done are a native Windows run, a re-run on Apple hardware and any iOS build. The workflows agree: the SDL_GPU leg of {{src:.github/workflows/d3d-windows-ci.yml|d3d-windows-ci.yml}} runs only on manual dispatch and is recorded as not run yet; {{src:.github/workflows/apple-ci.yml|apple-ci.yml}} gates a focused macOS smoke set ({{src:scripts/ci/run-sdlgpu-smoke.sh|run-sdlgpu-smoke.sh}}: device, swapchain, 2D drawing and a handful of conformance programs) that its own header calls “not the full SDL_GPU Apple qualification” and that handoff.md records as not run yet, and its iOS SDL_GPU legs are non-gating because SDL_GPU “has never been built for iOS by a recorded run”. added.title: An XNB BoundingSphere or Model mesh sphere with a negative radius fails to load, although XNA and CNA's own XNB writer accept it
added.summary: ContentReader::ReadBoundingSphere builds the sphere through the validating BoundingSphere(Vector3, float) constructor, so a negative radius in a .xnb throws System::ArgumentException, where XNA's reader assigns Center and Radius as stored.
added.public_contract: ContentManager::Load of an .xnb holding a BoundingSphere (BoundingSphereReader) or a Model (the per-mesh bounding sphere)
added.expected: XNA 4.0's ContentReader.ReadBoundingSphere reads the centre and the radius into the sphere's fields without a check, so content that stores a negative radius (a degenerate or hand-made asset) loads, and a Model's mesh bounds stay advisory. CNA's own XNB writer follows XNA here: it writes such a sphere rather than refusing it.
added.actual: At this snapshot {{src:modules/content/src/Xna/ContentReader.cpp|ContentReader::ReadBoundingSphere}} returns BoundingSphere(center, radius), and since e1377c437 that constructor ({{src:modules/math/src/BoundingSphere.cpp|BoundingSphere.cpp}}) throws System::ArgumentException for a negative radius. The Model reader takes each mesh's sphere through the same call ({{src:modules/content/src/Xnb/XnbModelGraphReader.hpp|XnbModelGraphReader.hpp}}), so one negative mesh radius fails the whole model load. The writer side accepts the same value on purpose: the fuzz seed “a bounding sphere with a negative radius and a NaN centre” in {{src:modules/content/tests/CNA/Internal/Xnb/XnbWriterInputFuzzTests.cpp|XnbWriterInputFuzzTests.cpp}} expects Outcome::Written (“XNA writes the sphere the content gave it, and a Model's own bounds are advisory”), so a file CNA writes can be one CNA cannot read back.

sources.note: ReadBoundingSphere constructs through BoundingSphere(Vector3, float)
the constructor throws System::ArgumentException for radius < 0 (e1377c437)
the Model reader reads each mesh's bounding sphere through ReadBoundingSphere
the writer accepts and writes a negative radius on purpose

added.evidence: Read at c6dec91f: the reader and constructor code above, and the writer fuzz seed that documents the XNA writer behaviour. XNA 4.0's reader behaviour was read in the XNA 4.0 Framework assembly (it assigns the two fields). Nothing was built or run for this entry; no test loads an .xnb with a negative radius.
added.tests_current: PrimitiveAndMathReaderTest.BoundingSphereReaderRoundTrips covers an ordinary sphere only; the writer fuzz test writes a negative radius but never reads it back.
added.regression_test: Read a BoundingSphereReader payload and a Model whose mesh sphere has radius -1 and assert that both load with the stored values, as in XNA.
added.blast_radius: Only content that stores a negative radius: degenerate or hand-made spheres and models exported with broken bounds. Normal pipeline output has non-negative radii.
added.workaround: Fix the radius in the source asset, or rebuild the content so the pipeline recomputes the bounds.

added.origin: new finding at the c6dec91f pin move: the storage repairs (21b4cd64c, CNA-DEMOS-ISSUE-152) call a sharp-runtime FileStream constructor that sharp-runtime added after its v0.1.0 tag
added.title: The sibling version check accepts sharp-runtime's v0.1.0 tag, but this snapshot needs sharp-runtime APIs added after it (a FileStream constructor and XmlSerializer property members), so such a build fails to compile instead of failing configuration
added.summary: cmake/DependencyVersions.cmake requires sharp-runtime 0.1.0 or a later 0.1.x patch, which the v0.1.0 tag satisfies, yet StorageContainer.cpp calls a FileStream constructor sharp-runtime gained in c6984ece and XmlSerializationEXT.hpp registers properties through MakeProperty, added in f990d074; the tag has neither, and sharp-runtime's next still declares 0.1.0.
added.public_contract: Configuring and building CNA at this snapshot against a sharp-runtime checkout that declares version 0.1.0 (CNA_CHECK_DEPENDENCY_VERSIONS, on by default)
added.expected: The configure-time version check exists so that a sibling checkout CNA cannot build against is refused before compilation, with the git checkout that fixes it. A sharp-runtime checkout it accepts should provide every API this CNA revision calls.
added.actual: {{src:cmake/DependencyVersions.cmake|DependencyVersions.cmake}} sets CNA_REQUIRED_SHARP_RUNTIME_VERSION to 0.1.0, and sharp-runtime's v0.1.0 tag declares exactly that, so configuration passes. {{src:modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp|StorageContainer.cpp}} opens container files through System::IO::FileStream(path, mode, access, share) (the FileShare honouring of CNA-DEMOS-ISSUE-152); that four-argument constructor is not in sharp-runtime's v0.1.0 (its FileStream.hpp has the one- and two-argument forms) and arrived in sharp-runtime commit c6984ece, which is on its next branch. Since bbed8c61e {{src:modules/math/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/XmlSerializationEXT.hpp|XmlSerializationEXT.hpp}} also registers the properties of Color and Rectangle through System::Xml::Serialization::detail::MakeProperty, which sharp-runtime added in f990d074 (2026-10-24), after c6984ece; the header is included by CNA's math XML serialization tests, compiled into CnaTests, and by any game that serializes those types. A build against the tag therefore fails in the compiler with no configure-time message, and one against a next revision between the two commits builds the libraries but not CnaTests. The version stayed 0.1.0 on sharp-runtime's next, so the check cannot tell the two apart.

added.origin: new finding at the 3b43bd86 pin move: handoff.md section 5.2 newly lists FNA3D-MISSING-STOCK-INPUT for PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect (measured by the museum's rv-shading on 2026-10-25); the refusal itself dates from 84bf6fc4a (AM4-190)
added.title: FNA3D refuses a PbrEffect or SkinnedPbrEffect draw whose vertex declaration has no Tangent0 on its SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11 drivers, where every other renderer draws it with a neutral tangent
added.summary: FNA3D's SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11 drivers cannot build a pipeline for a shader input the declaration lacks, so the FNA3D renderer throws NotSupportedException (FNA3D-MISSING-STOCK-INPUT) for a PBR draw over tangent-free vertices such as VertexPositionNormalTexture; its OpenGL driver and the other renderers supply a neutral tangent.
added.public_contract: PbrEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect (CNAEXT) draws on the FNA3D renderer with a VertexDeclaration that has no Tangent element at usage index 0, when FNA3D runs its SDL_GPU or Direct3D 11 driver
added.expected: Since 91612a0a3 (museum rv-shading, 2026-10-22) CNA's PBR effects do not depend on whether a mesh stores a tangent: a renderer supplies the neutral tangent the GL path reads for an absent input, and {{src:modules/graphics/examples/pbr_vertex_contract_test.cpp|pbr_vertex_contract_test.cpp}} draws the same surface from VertexPositionNormalTexture and from VertexPositionNormalTangentTexture. A tangent-free mesh should draw the same on every renderer that ships PbrEffect.
added.actual: Before it binds the vertex buffers of a stock draw, {{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dDraw.cpp|Fna3dDraw.cpp}} checks that every input the selected effect variant reads is declared (RequireStockVertexInputsDeclared); for CnaPbrEffect and CnaSkinnedPbrEffect that includes Tangent0. A missing input throws System::NotSupportedException (“FNA3D renderer (FNA3D-MISSING-STOCK-INPUT): ... FNA3D's SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11 drivers cannot create a pipeline for it (only its OpenGL driver reads a default for a missing input)”). The check is skipped only where the driver reads a default, which {{src:modules/renderers/fna3d/src/Fna3dRenderer.cpp|Fna3dRenderer.cpp}} records for FNA3D's OpenGL driver alone (driverDefaultsMissingVertexInputs_). FNA3D tries its SDL_GPU driver first ({{src:docs/fna3d-renderer.md|fna3d-renderer.md}}), so on a default FNA3D device a PBR draw over a tangent-free declaration, such as XNA's VertexPositionNormalTexture, throws, where FNA3D's OpenGL driver and every other renderer supply a neutral tangent. CNA lists the limitation in {{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2.
