added.origin: new finding at the 3b43bd86 pin move: handoff.md section 5.2 newly records MojoShader's SPIR-V refusal of ps_1_4 BEM and TEXDEPTH (2026-10-26 dependency audit, c8b8e0aa0); the other six instructions were found by reading the MojoShader fork at 03b686fe1a33
added.title: Compiled XNA effects whose pixel shaders use BEM, TEXDEPTH, TEXDP3, TEXDP3TEX, TEXM3X2DEPTH or TEXREG2AR/GB/RGB cannot run on SDL_GPU, WEBGPU or FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver
added.summary: MojoShader's SPIR-V profile, which CNA's SDL_GPU and WEBGPU compiled effects and FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver use, refuses these eight shader model 1.x instructions by name ('... unimplemented in spirv profile'); its GLSL profile translates them, so the same effects run on EasyGL and on FNA3D's OpenGL driver.
added.public_contract: Compiled XNA 4.0 effects (Effect from .xnb or .fxb) whose pixel shaders use the shader model 1.x instructions BEM, TEXDEPTH, TEXDP3, TEXDP3TEX, TEXM3X2DEPTH, TEXREG2AR, TEXREG2GB or TEXREG2RGB, on the SDL_GPU and WEBGPU compiled-effect routes and on the FNA3D renderer's SDL_GPU driver
added.expected: A compiled effect XNA 4.0 runs should run on every renderer that reports GraphicsCapability::CompiledEffects, or be refused with its reason up front. CNA's EasyGL and SOFTWARE compiled-effect routes execute the complete pixel shader model 1.x instruction set ({{src:docs/software-easygl-parity-ledger.md|software-easygl-parity-ledger.md}}), and the bump-environment work of this snapshot (725481a1e) made a pass's BUMPENVMAT state reach FNA3D's drivers.
added.actual: In the MojoShader fork CNA builds (libcna/mojoshader at 03b686fe1a33, the revision the pinned FNA3D fork records; {{src:cmake/ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake|ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake}}), profiles/mojoshader_profile_spirv.c declares BEM, TEXDEPTH, TEXDP3, TEXDP3TEX, TEXM3X2DEPTH, TEXREG2AR, TEXREG2GB and TEXREG2RGB through EMIT_SPIRV_OPCODE_UNIMPLEMENTED_FUNC, which fails the translation with “op unimplemented in spirv profile”. The GLSL profile implements all eight (the comment above the SPIR-V list, “unimplemented even in the GLSL emitter”, is out of date). The SPIR-V profile is the one CNA's SDL_GPU compiled effects use, the one CNA's WEBGPU compiled effects translate to WGSL from, and the one FNA3D's SDL_GPU driver uses; {{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2 (“MojoShader SPIR-V gaps”) records the refusal for the ps_1_4 BEM and TEXDEPTH, and the six ps_1_2/ps_1_3 texture-addressing instructions take the same failure path. An effect that uses any of them runs on EasyGL's and SOFTWARE's compiled effects and on FNA3D's OpenGL driver, but cannot run on SDL_GPU (the default renderer on Windows, macOS and iOS), on WEBGPU, or on FNA3D with its default SDL_GPU driver.

added.origin: new finding at the 3b43bd86 pin move: handoff.md section 5.2 lists two defects of the MojoShader code behind FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver found in the third round of the 2026-10-26 dependency-audit review (R9-01, R9-03) and left unfixed; the integer-rewrite half was confirmed in the pinned libcna/mojoshader source
added.title: FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver cannot build some valid compiled effects: a ps_3_0 shader that reads two vertex outputs packed in one register fails to compile, and the integer input-layout rewrite can retype the wrong semantic
added.summary: the MojoShader code behind FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver, in CNA's pinned fork, names a struct member that does not exist when a ps_3_0 shader reads, from one register, semantics the vertex shader wrote to separate registers, so the generated HLSL fails to compile; and it finds the semantic of an integer vertex element by substring, so DEPTH1 can match an earlier DEPTH10 and swap their integer and float declarations.
added.public_contract: Compiled XNA effects (Effect Framework bytecode) drawn on the FNA3D renderer when FNA3D runs its Direct3D 11 driver (Windows; FNA3D tries its SDL_GPU driver first, or the driver is selected with FNA3D_FORCE_DRIVER)
added.expected: A compiled effect that Direct3D 9 runs should run on every FNA3D driver: a vertex shader may write the semantics a ps_3_0 pixel shader reads in any register layout, and an integer vertex element should change the declaration of exactly the semantic it names.
added.actual: The FNA3D renderer builds FNA3D and MojoShader from CNA’s forks ({{src:cmake/ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake|ThirdPartyFNA3D.cmake}}, MojoShader 03b686fe1a33). In that MojoShader, the code behind FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver (mojoshader_d3d11.c) links a vertex shader’s output struct to the pixel shader’s input struct by name; when a ps_3_0 shader reads two semantics packed into one register (FOG in its x, TEXCOORD0 in yzw, both from v0) that the vertex shader wrote to separate registers (o1.x, o2.yzw), the generated HLSL names a member that does not exist and does not compile (R9-01; CNA records it as present before the review too). When the input layout has an integer element, the same file rewrites the declaration of its semantic in the HLSL source by locating <name><index> with strstr, so DEPTH1 is found inside an earlier DEPTH10 and the integer and float declarations of the two are swapped (R9-03). CNA lists both in {{src:handoff.md|handoff.md}} section 5.2 as found in the review’s third round and not fixed, and notes that CNA’s committed effects contain neither shape. The same section records that the rewrite looks for PSIZE0 where the generated HLSL writes PSIZE.

added.evidence: Read at 3b43bd86: the handoff entry and the pin. In the pinned fork (03b686fe1a33, read in a local clone of libcna/mojoshader) the integer rewrite builds the semantic name with snprintf(sem, ..., "%s%d", SemanticName, SemanticIndex) and locates it with strstr(newSource, sem), which matches a prefix of a longer name. The ps_3_0 packing case rests on CNA’s record of the review, not on a reproduction here. Nothing was built or executed for this entry; no run on Windows is recorded for either case.
added.tests_current: No test in CNA or in the fork’s tests/cna covers either shape; FNA3D’s Direct3D 11 driver runs the fork’s eight test executables under Wine with DXVK (recorded by CNA), none with an integer DEPTH1/DEPTH10 pair or a packed ps_3_0 input.
added.regression_test: A fork test that compiles, through the code behind FNA3D's Direct3D 11 driver, a ps_3_0 shader reading FOG and TEXCOORD0 from one register against a vertex shader writing them separately, and a vertex declaration with integer DEPTH1 beside float DEPTH10; both must link with the declarations they name.
added.blast_radius: Games that load custom compiled effects of those shapes and run on the FNA3D renderer with its Direct3D 11 driver. CNA’s committed effects, FNA3D’s OpenGL and SDL_GPU drivers, and the other renderers are unaffected.
added.workaround: Use FNA3D’s SDL_GPU or OpenGL driver (the FNA3D_FORCE_DRIVER hint) or another renderer for such effects, or give the vertex shader the register packing the pixel shader reads and avoid semantics whose names are prefixes of each other.

added.origin: new finding at the 3b43bd86 pin move (Deep Dives review, confirmed by the coordinator): RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask (35, c7f6c68e5, CNA-DEMOS DC-R2) answers against what two renderer configurations do with a mask
added.title: RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask misreports EasyGL without glSampleMaski (OPENGLES3 on an OpenGL ES 3.0 context, WEBGL2) and WEBGPU over wgpu-native's Metal driver
added.summary: The feature is defined so that Unsupported means a mask has no effect and Supported means any mask is applied, but EasyGL without glSampleMaski answers Unsupported while it throws NotSupportedException for every mask other than all ones, and WEBGPU over wgpu-native's Metal driver answers Supported while it refuses a partial mask; a program that trusts the answer either fails at the draw or never learns that the mask is refused.
added.public_contract: GraphicsDevice::GetRendererFeatureSupportEXT(CNA::RendererFeature::MultiSampleMask) and the C constant CNA_RENDERER_FEATURE_MULTI_SAMPLE_MASK, against BlendState/GraphicsDevice MultiSampleMask on a multisampled target
added.expected: {{src:modules/graphics/include/CNA/RendererCapabilityProfile.hpp|RendererCapabilityProfile.hpp}} defines the answers: Supported, any mask selects the samples a draw writes; Restricted, only a mask that keeps every sample or none is applied and any other is refused with NotSupportedException; Unsupported, the mask has no effect. The answer should describe what the renderer then does.
added.actual: {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/EasyGL/EasyGLRenderer.hpp|EasyGLRenderer.hpp}} answers Unsupported when the context has no glSampleMaski (desktop GL before 3.2, OpenGL ES 3.0, WebGL 2), but ApplyBlendState in {{src:modules/renderers/easygl/src/EasyGLRenderer.cpp|EasyGLRenderer.cpp}} throws NotSupportedException (“BlendState.MultiSampleMask requires desktop GL 3.2 or OpenGL ES 3.1”) for every mask other than all ones there, a mask of none included: the mask is not without effect, it is refused. {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/WebGPU/WebGPURenderer.hpp|WebGPURenderer.hpp}} answers Supported whenever a device exists, while {{src:modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp|WebGPURenderer.cpp}} (SupportsPartialMultiSampleMaskEXT, false on WGPUBackendType_Metal) refuses a partial mask on wgpu-native’s Metal driver, whose pipelines have no sample mask; by the definition above that is Restricted.

sources.note: MultiSampleMask = 35: the meaning of Supported, Restricted and Unsupported
MultiSampleMaskSupportEXT: Unsupported without glSampleMaski
ApplyBlendState: NotSupportedException for a mask other than all ones without glSampleMaski
MultiSampleMaskSupportEXT: Supported whenever a device exists
SupportsPartialMultiSampleMaskEXT false on wgpu-native's Metal driver; RecordDrawOrder refuses a partial mask there
MultiSampleMaskSupportMatchesWhatTheResolvedTargetShows: would fail in both configurations, which CNA's recorded runs do not include

added.evidence: Checked by reading at 3b43bd86; not executed. The cross-renderer test that holds the answer to the behaviour (MultiSampleMaskSupportMatchesWhatTheResolvedTargetShows) draws with masks all, none and one: on an EasyGL context without glSampleMaski its mask-0 draw would throw, and on WEBGPU over wgpu-native's Metal driver its partial-mask draw would throw where a Supported renderer must resolve a quarter of the red.
